newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Bargain-hunting fuels Singapore shares, ignore Deng.
newsitem.headline: Bargain-hunting fuels Singapore shares, ignore Deng.

text.p: Bargain-hunting lifted the Singapore stock market to end higher on Thursday.
After a brief weakness at the open on news of the death of Chinese leader, Deng Xiaoping, the market recovered and rallied on bargain-hunting, dealers said.
"People took the opportunity to dredge for value among the stocks as the market took Deng's death in stride," said a dealer with a local brokerage house.
Activity was centred on electronic shares listed on the second board, SESDAQ, driven by sentiment, dealers said.
He said sentiment was buoyed by Singapore's and Malaysia's push towards high-technology industries.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 4.99 points or 0.22 percent at 2,251.98 while the UOB SESDAQ index ended up 4.44 percent up at 119.40.

Recently listed stocks, most of which are small-capitalised firms, saw keen retail interest. These included seafood company Pacific Andes and fruit supplier FHTK which topped the actives with over 28.7 million and 19.5 million shares respectively.
Speculative Malaysian counters like Berjaya Group and Kemayan Industries were also active. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
